nodes.title: Drinfeld modules
nodes.statement: Fix a finite field F of size q, a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/F, a closed point ∞ of degree δ, A=Γ(C−∞,O_C), and an F-algebra field L with characteristic map γ:A→L. A Drinfeld module is an F-algebra map φ:A→L{τ} with ∂φ_a=γ(a), not equal to the scalar map C∘γ. The q-Frobenius Ore ring and its identification with F-linear polynomial group endomorphisms are supplied by FF.4. The characteristic is ker γ; generic characteristic means γ injective. The rank theorem below supplies r rather than imposing a potentially circular definition.

proofSteps: Import the FF.4 composition-ring comparison.
Define the characteristic using the constant-coefficient homomorphism; evaluate on every commutative L-algebra to obtain the group-scheme action.
Use the rank theorem to reconcile this field definition with constant positive rank.

The action on group-scheme points is natural in the value algebra.

nodes.title: The characteristic-place realization
nodes.statement: Fix a characteristic prime p, residue field F_p of size qhat=q^f, an F_p-algebra R, and a characteristic map A→R whose local uniformizer image is nilpotent. nodes.title: Generalized Drinfeld modules
nodes.statement: A generalized Drinfeld A-module of rank ≤r over S is a line bundle E with an F-linear A-action, differential γ, every field fiber a Drinfeld module of positive rank ≤r, and the global degree bound φ_a=Σ_{i=0}^{r deg_A(a)}b_iτ^i. Define field-fiber positivity and weak separation independently of level.

nodes.title: Local algebraization of motive maps
nodes.statement: Let L be finitely generated over F. Put K_0,L=Frac(K_0⊗F L), K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L), and L_(λ)=Frac((F_λ⊗F L)[[z]]). A restricted module means a finite projective module with invertible Frobenius linearization; at λ it has a finite-projective integral lattice with invertible Frobenius. Extension K_0,L→K_0,λ,L is K_0,λ/K_0-fully faithful on such modules and preserves semisimple objects. Extension K_0,λ,L→L_(λ) is fully faithful on the λ-restricted objects and preserves semisimple objects. Thus completed Frobenius-equivariant maps are algebraized over the rational coefficient ring. The first ring is not the full completed Laurent-series ring unless L is finite.
hypotheses: Finitely generated coefficient field L, hence finitely many roots of unity; K_0,λ/K_0 separable; the λ-restricted integral model condition is explicit.

Frac for the split completed coefficient algebra denotes its total quotient ring, with every residue-field factor retained; it is generally a product of fields. The rational scalar extension K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L) is not replaced by the full Laurent-series completion.
proofSteps: For scalar extension, reduce to finite and one-variable transcendental extensions; Frobenius-fixed denominators descend to the constant field.
Prove separability of the function-field completion by a separating local parameter.
Use the period ring and its two fixed-ring identities to construct a full faithful left-adjoint realization functor.
Every invariant subobject is quasigeometric; the descended lattice supplies the λ-restricted condition.
acceptance: When L is finite the two local coefficient rings agree; for positive transcendence degree they need not.

nodes.title: The Tate period ring
nodes.statement: For finitely generated L/F choose a projective normal F-model X of its function field and compatible extensions of each prime-divisor valuation to L^sep. Inside L_(λ)^sep, let B⁺ be the Laurent series whose coefficients have valuation bounded below at every compatible prime divisor and are integral outside a finite set of divisors of X. Let S consist of invertible integral local series s with σ(s)/s∈K_0,λ⊗F L. Set B=B⁺[S⁻¹]. It has B^σ=K_0,λ and B^G_L=K_0,λ,L, contains every τ-fixed solution of a λ-restricted finite-rank system, and yields B⊗_(K_0,λ) V_λ(M)≅B⊗_(K_0,λ,L)M. Full completion cannot replace B in the algebraization argument.
hypotheses: L finitely generated over F; normal proper model; valuation extensions normalized by ramification; finite residue factors retained; σ is q-coefficient Frobenius fixing z.

Frac for the split completed coefficient algebra denotes its total quotient ring, with every residue-field factor retained; it is generally a product of fields. The rational scalar extension K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L) is not replaced by the full Laurent-series completion.

Projective normal finite-type F-models exist by projective closure and finite normalization. Transcendence degree need not be one; bounded-pole section spaces use proper coherent finiteness in any dimension.
proofSteps: Choose a projective normal F-model, of any transcendence degree. Cover the finitely many exceptional prime-divisor supports by an effective Cartier divisor using a nonzero homogeneous section of a projective embedding, and raise its power to bound the coefficient poles. The coefficients then lie in H^0(X,O_X(nD)), finite-dimensional by proper coherent finiteness (SF.2/ample-serre-vanishing with a chosen ample line). A curve-only Riemann–Roch statement is not used for higher-dimensional models.
Construct integral Frobenius units and invert them; the formal functional equations move all solutions into B.
Prove the σ-fixed and Galois-fixed ring identities before applying invariant tensor arguments.
The semilinear fixed-vector basis gives the comparison isomorphism. The construction and properties are proved in Stalder §6, not posited as fields in a structure.

nodes.title: Finite-field nuclear determinants
nodes.statement: Let V be a compact topological F-vector space. A continuous F-linear endomorphism is locally contracting if on some open invariant subspace U its norm decreases by a constant c<1. For Φ=Σ_(n≥1)φ_nZ^n with locally contracting coefficients define det_(F[[Z]])(1+Φ|V) modulo Z^N using a common contracting nucleus for φ₁,…,φ_(N−1) and the determinant on the finite quotient V/U; the compatible residues define the series. It is independent of the common nuclei for the fixed norm. Exact-sequence multiplicativity holds. For continuous endomorphisms a,b, Taelman’s cyclic theorem gives det(1−abZ)=det(1−baZ) when a, ab and ba are all locally contracting; the plus-sign variant follows by replacing a by −a. No arbitrary-series cyclic theorem or unrestricted norm-invariance assertion is made. This finite-field compact-vector-space theory differs from the complex Banach nuclear-operator theory already owned by OperatorTheory.
hypotheses: F finite; compact V; continuous endomorphisms; norm/topology chosen as in Taelman §2; each coefficient locally contracting and no constant coefficient.
The compact F-vector space is normed, with its nonarchimedean norm inducing the topology and the trivial norm on F. Local contraction is measured in this norm.
proofSteps: Every finite coefficient list admits a common nucleus.
On a smaller common nucleus, the contracting piece contributes determinant one modulo the required power of Z.
Finite-dimensional determinant identities descend to the inverse limit of truncations.
Prove invariance under equivalent compact norms and functorial conjugation.

For the cyclic law apply Taelman Theorem 2 with its three contraction assumptions. Its proof chooses common nuclei and bounds the intermediate images; nuclearity of the two products alone is not the cited hypothesis.
acceptance: For finite-dimensional V, recover the ordinary determinant.

sources.locator: Definitions 3–5 and Propositions 6–10, pp. 377–379; Theorem 2, p. 380

nodes.statement: For R and K_∞ in the integral-model setting, a finite projective R-module M with q-Frobenius-semilinear τ_M, and Θ∈R{τ}[[Z]]·τZ acting through τ_M, the product over maximal ideals satisfies ∏_m det(1+Θ|M/mM)=det(1+Θ|(M⊗R K_∞)/M)⁻¹. The right-hand coefficients are nuclear. Both sides converge in F[[Z]]. The Frobenius-divisibility condition on Θ is essential; scalar multiplication alone is not this trace formula.

proofSteps: Prove local contraction for positive-Frobenius operators on the compact quotient.
Use localization exact sequences to isolate finite primes.
Apply Anderson’s commutator factorization to reduce arbitrary nuclear Θ to finite local factors.
Use determinant exactness/cyclic invariance to pass to the Euler product.

A continuous F-linear map γ:M₁→M₂ is N-tangent to the identity on V if, on some open U⊂V avoiding both lattices, its V/Λ₂ component restricts to an isometry and its local lift obeys ‖γ(v)−v‖≤‖θ^(−N)‖‖v‖. It is infinitely tangent if this holds for every N≥1, with U allowed to vary. For a continuous F-linear isomorphism γ define Δ_γ=Σ_(n≥1)(θ−γ⁻¹tγ)θ^(n−1)T^(−n) on M₁, where θ denotes the source t-action in this operator formula.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional local V, full lattices, finite H_i; local comparison in quotient charts; γ need not be A-linear.
proofSteps: Define the local lifts after avoiding lattice translates and require the isometry explicitly.
The differential-one entire exponential is infinitely tangent by shrinking its inverse-function neighborhood for each N.
Transport t-actions across γ to obtain the operator series.

nodes.title: Carlitz and a nonzero class module
nodes.statement: For Carlitz over F[θ], H=0, U=A log_C(1), and L(C/A)=ζ_A(1)=log_C(1), after renaming θ as T. For q=2, define E_t=θ+θ³τ over F₂[θ]. Then exp_E(x)=θ⁻³exp_C(θ³x), U_E=(π/θ³)A, H_E≅F₂[t]/(t), and L(E/A)=ι(π/θ²). The class is represented by θ⁻¹ and t annihilates it. Thus |H_E|=T is indispensable.
hypotheses: First example the Carlitz integral model; second q=2, K=F₂(θ), R=F₂[θ], π the DM.2 period lying in K_∞ in this case.
proofSteps: At q=2, ‖π‖=4 and π∈K_∞. Reduce any x modulo πA to degree ≤1 by cancelling leading terms.
On the degree-≤1 ball, exp_C is an isometric bijection: higher terms are strictly smaller, and the complete-field contraction argument gives its inverse. Hence exp_C(K_∞)=θF₂[[θ⁻¹]].
Scalar conjugation by θ³ yields exp_E(K_∞)=θ⁻²F₂[[θ⁻¹]]. Its intersection with A is zero, and the quotient modulo A has the single basis class θ⁻¹.
E_t(θ⁻¹)=1+θ lies in A, proving H_E≅A/(t); the unit lattice is θ⁻³ker exp_C.

Away from (θ), the reduction is conjugate to Carlitz; at (θ), its local factor is one. Thus L(E/A)=ζ_A(1)(T−1)/T=ι(π/θ²), also matching regulator times T. The period relation at q=2 is π=(θ²+θ)log_C(1), obtained from the Carlitz torsion equation and the monic product normalization.

nodes.title: Elliptic sheaves on the global curve
nodes.statement: On C×F S put σ=id_C×Frob_q,S. A rank-r elliptic sheaf consists of vector bundles E_i, i∈Z, and injections j_i:E_i→E_(i+1), τ_i:σ*E_i→E_(i+1), satisfying j_(i+1)τ_i=τ_(i+1)σ*j_i and a compatible periodicity E_(i+rδ)≅E_i(∞). Each j_i cokernel is supported on ∞×S and its pushforward to S is a line bundle; each τ_i cokernel is supported on the graph of the characteristic c:S→C−∞ and its pushforward is a line bundle. Maps are bounded-shift compatible chain maps E_i→E′_(i+n), with n≥0 independent of i, identified under further j-shifts. For the Drinfeld correspondence use the normalized/transverse subcategory below. These are bundles on the original global curve C.
hypotheses: C smooth projective geometrically connected over F; ∞ closed of degree δ; r≥1; characteristic leg disjoint from ∞; coherent injections and finite-flat length-one cokernels as specified.
proofSteps: Import native coherent locally free sheaves and effective divisor twists from the existing AlgebraicVectorBundles and AlgebraicCurves roadmaps via SF.0.
Build the integer-indexed periodic diagram with the Frobenius pullback and its commutative squares.
Define bounded-shift morphisms and compose by adding shifts; fixed-index maps alone miss nonconstant Drinfeld isogenies.
acceptance: For rational ∞ and rank one, E_(i+1)=E_i(∞); for rank two, E_(i+2)=E_i(∞).

Check the characteristic quotient and transverse squares; sections recover the τ-degree filtration and the normalized cohomology.

nodes.title: The normalized elliptic-sheaf dictionary
nodes.statement: The contravariant filtered-motive construction gives an anti-equivalence between standard relative Drinfeld A-modules of rank r and normalized transverse elliptic sheaves of rank r with bounded-shift morphisms. The inverse uses the line (pr_S*E_0)∨ and the Ore module Γ((C−∞)×S,E_0), locally free of rank one over O_S{τ}; right A-action reconstructs the Drinfeld map. Equivalently, this is a covariant equivalence with the opposite elliptic-sheaf category; no self-duality identification of that category is asserted. Characteristic and rank are preserved, and good-open level structures transport through the finite-shtuka pairing.
hypotheses: The normalized/transverse/disjoint-leg conditions and morphism convention above; standard relative Drinfeld objects.
proofSteps: Use the normalized cohomology to identify the generator line and its Frobenius iterates.
The affine sections form the Ore module; multiplication by a∈A respects the filtration and has unit leading term.
Construct the inverse action locally and descend the line-bundle maps.
The two constructions recover the same filtered module; evaluate the morphism maps to verify reversed composition and natural inverse isomorphisms.
acceptance: The generator of sections is dual to the point-line generator, as in the motive functor.

nodes.statement: From the elliptic chain take E_0 and α=j_0⁻¹τ_0:σ*E_0|_U≅E_0|_U, where U=(C×S)−((∞×S)∪Γ_c). The τ- and j-cokernels provide the characteristic zero and infinity pole bounds of a GL_r-modification. At rational ∞ they are length-one modifications; at general δ the pole support and residue factors are retained as the specified infinity chain rather than replaced by a rational leg. Export this datum to the independently defined global G-shtuka category in GS.2. The global category does not supply elliptic sheaves back to this construction.

Pass from the rank-r vector bundle to its GL_r frame torsor using existing vector-bundle APIs.
Record the two modifications with their cokernels and preserve levels by restriction.
GS.2 consumes the resulting datum; no dependency on its elliptic-sheaf-realisation node is introduced.

nodes.title: Prime-to-characteristic realization comparison
nodes.statement: For a normalized elliptic sheaf attached to E and λ away from the characteristic, complete its affine motive M at λ. Its τ-fixed completed realization is canonically dual to T_λE, with the A_λ-linear Galois pairing obtained at each λ^n level from the finite-shtuka functor. The pairing is compatible with all Drinfeld morphisms, bounded shifts of elliptic-chain maps, base extension and prime-to-characteristic level frames.
hypotheses: Field coefficient L for Galois realization, λ away from ker γ; full completed residue factors; contravariant motive convention.
proofSteps: Reduce M modulo λ^n and apply the strict finite-shtuka/group-scheme anti-equivalence.
Identify the torsion points with the dual Frobenius-fixed module by the evaluation pairing.
Pass through the chosen division coordinates to the Tate limit and duality.
acceptance: For Carlitz the point Tate character and the motive-fixed character are inverse, as required by the pairing.

nodes.title: The effective characteristic local comparison
nodes.statement: For characteristic p and an F_p-algebra R with nilpotent uniformizer image γ(z), completing the affine motive of the elliptic sheaf and selecting the characteristic residue factor gives the same rank-r effective local shtuka as DM.1, with q^(deg p)-Frobenius and the dimension-one cokernel bound. Its finite reductions correspond to the full p-power strict finite group schemes. This is a comparison of completed motives and finite torsion, not a characteristic-place rank-r separable-point Tate representation or an unrestricted crystalline/étale comparison.
hypotheses: Nilpotent characteristic parameter; residue coefficient algebra F_p; all completion/splitting and effectiveness hypotheses of DM.1/characteristic-local-realization; the exact equal-characteristic category is a recorded input, with a locally free R[[z]]-module and a rank-one R-cokernel killed by z−γ(z).
proofSteps: Identify affine motive restrictions through the elliptic dictionary.
Complete and split coefficient factors; iterate τ by the residue degree.
Apply the same strict finite-group correspondence used in DM.1, retaining connected torsion and its bound.
acceptance: For φ_t=τ² over F, connected length q^(2n) at level t^n is preserved under this comparison.
